articles.title: Septuagenarians versus octogenarians in elective upper extremity procedures.
articles.authors: Ku PH, Nur Y, Sasaki J, Richards M, Parisier E, Uddin A, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national database
articles.population: People aged 70-89 years undergoing elective shoulder surgery
articles.outcomes: Unplanned readmission, non-home discharge, overall complications, reoperation, and 30-day mortality
articles.take_home: People aged 80-89 years having elective shoulder surgery were more likely to need unplanned readmission to hospital and to be discharged to care facilities rather than home, compared to those aged 70-79 years. However, rates of surgical complications and death within 30 days were similar between the two age groups.

articles.title: Inadequate cervicothoracic assessment is nearly universal for screening participants with lateral elbow tendinopathy: A systematic review of 208 randomized controlled trials.
articles.authors: Schumacher MR, Bakken EK, Reynolds KP, Elletson DR, Eckert JL
articles.study_type: Systematic review of randomised controlled trials
articles.outcomes: Adequacy of cervicothoracic spine screening methods before diagnosing lateral elbow tendinopathy
articles.take_home: Almost all studies examining treatments for lateral elbow tendinopathy failed to properly check whether the neck and upper back were contributing to the problem, with only 1.9% of trials doing thorough screening. This suggests research into lateral elbow tendinopathy may be missing an important part of the picture.
